verdict.rationale: Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol provides RFC 9421 HTTP message signatures with agent-browser-auth/agent-payer-auth tags, timestamps/nonces to prevent replay, and verification against Visa's published JWKS, explicitly designed so merchants can 'instantly distinguish a legitimate, credentialed agent from an anonymous bot.' This is reinforced by agent-scoped credentials, passkey-anchored consent, and a public reference implementation (agent-registry, cdn-proxy verification) merchants can run. Community commentary notes standardized agent-identity is still an open industry problem generally, but doesn't contradict that Visa's specific signature/trust-tier mechanism works as documented. missing for 10: independent/hands-on merchant verification reports beyond Visa's own repo and docs, and clarity on real-world adoption/maturity given the 'in development' caveat.
